body:
I've recently read a [post](https://www.reddit.com/r/C_Programming/comments/16vh3n7/what_is_the_maximum_recommended_size_for_a_stack) about avoiding stack allocation of any value above 1024 bytes.

For reference, I got [this comment](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/115235#discussion_r2784280276) from an earlier PR of mine where I wanted something to allocate 4096 bytes.

Ah. I'm not too knowledgeable about C++ stack or heap allocations.

What should I replace it with? A `new` heap allocation?

I chose a 64KiB buffer because reading 1 byte at a time would likely be much slower.
My two suggestions would be either a smaller buffer (1024 bytes should be mostly OK on the stack and may be fast enough) or using a `LocalVector`, which is allocated on the heap.

I think I will use a `LocalVector` then, because these methods are already reading/writing files so the overhead of heap-allocating is expected. But the user will want the compress/uncompress to happen as fast as possible, and a larger buffer should make a difference.
I changed it to use `LocalVector` with `.resize()` and `.ptr()`. Please let me know if I did it wrong.
